deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a heavily corrected draft of Riemann's speculative psychology and natural philosophy, the 'Geistesmassen' (mental masses) theory continued from the previous page. In the left column he redrafts this several times; the right column is a cleaner fair copy. The argument runs as follows.

(1) Excitation of related masses. Excitation spreads not only to Geistesmassen related to a newly formed one. It also spreads indirectly to those connected with them, i.e. bound to them in earlier acts. A subgroup of related masses that is internally connected is therefore excited both directly and indirectly, and so relatively more strongly than the rest. The right column adds that indirect excitation is weaker the more remotely, and the more weakly among themselves, the masses are connected.

(2) Reproduction. The activity of an older Geistesmasse shows itself first in reproduction: the acting mass strives to produce one similar to itself.

(3) Interaction is materially mediated. The interaction of two simultaneously forming masses depends on a material process between the places where they are formed. Masses in immediate interaction bind to one another according to the degree of that interaction.

(4) Formation of new masses. New masses arise partly from the activity of older masses and partly from external, material causes. Everything acting together inhibits or favours itself according to the inner difference or likeness of the masses it strives to produce. This is a Herbart-style law of inhibition and promotion, stated qualitatively.

(5) Application to explaining life on Earth. Masses produced in nerve processes persist unchanged as parts of the soul. Their inner connection is changed only by entering new connections. A parenthetical empirical aside says that masses which appear simple are produced in a nerve process lasting about 1/10 to 1/9 second in a single primitive fibre.

An immediate consequence is that the souls of organisms persist after death. To explain the planned, cumulative development of organic nature, Riemann postulates that these souls enter a larger unified Geistesmasse, apparently the Erdseele (Earth-soul). There they lead a higher mental life under the same laws, just as nerve-generated masses do in our own soul. The page ends with the beginning of an example of masses from many primitive fibres combining into one, and the marginal note 'Ihr isolirtes Fortbestehen genügt nicht' (their isolated persistence is not sufficient), which leads to the next page's discussion of the Earth-soul and its seat beneath the crust.

There is nothing quantitative to reconstruct beyond the 1/10 to 1/9 s figure.
errors: No mathematical steps, so no mathematical errors. The physiological figure of 1/10 to 1/9 s per elementary nerve process is an empirical estimate of the period, comparable in order of magnitude to contemporary reaction-time and nerve-conduction work (Helmholtz 1850). It is not derived here.
The doctrine of the persistence of the soul after death and of the Earth-soul is metaphysical speculation in the manner of Fechner and Herbart. It is not a scientifically justified inference.

results.what: Laws of association of 'Geistesmassen': spreading excitation through connected masses, reproduction as a mass striving to produce a similar one, and mutual inhibition or promotion according to likeness or difference
results.modern_name: Associationist psychology / Herbartian 'Vorstellungsmechanik' (a precursor of spreading-activation models)
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (1820s), with Riemann explicitly building on him

results.what: Persistence of souls after death and their union into an Earth-soul that explains the purposive development of organic nature
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Zend-Avesta, 1851); Riemann's version appears in the published 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' (Gesammelte Werke, ed. Weber, 1876)

results.what: Duration of an elementary nerve process of about 1/10 to 1/9 second in a primitive fibre
results.usually_credited_to: Contemporary physiology (Helmholtz and others); unsure whether this exact figure appears in Riemann's published fragments

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft versions of Riemann's known natural-philosophy fragments on Geistesmassen and the Earth-soul, published in substance in the Gesammelte Werke. There is no mathematics. Only the textual variants and the 1/10 to 1/9 s aside are of minor interest.

checkable.asserts: The stated duration range for an elementary nerve process is well ordered: 0.1 s to about 0.111 s.
The width of the stated interval is about 0.0111 s.

transcription_corrections: The first word is most likely 'Diese' ('Diese Erregung erstreckt sich aber nicht blos auf die verwandten Geistesmassen...').
'in früheren Acten' may read 'in früheren Denkacten'; uncertain.

The marginal note in the right column, 'Ihr ewiges[?] Fortbestehen genügt nicht', more plausibly reads 'Ihr isolirtes Fortbestehen genügt nicht'. This fits the next page's argument that the masses must be united.
In the fraction 1/10 to 1/9 the denominators appear overwritten in the manuscript; the reading 1/10 to 1/9 is plausible but not certain.
'einer vollen[?] Reihe' is doubtful; the line has a heavily corrected passage beginning 'bei diesen Wesen'.
The right column is a fair copy of the left-column drafts (interaction mediated by a material process; reproduction; inhibition or promotion by likeness), numbered '1)' for the final formulation.
